# Cade Mini

> A small, durable coding agent built on one append-only session log.

# Cade Mini

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Cade Mini

Cade Mini is a standalone coding agent. It keeps one rule at the center of the
design:

> The session log is the source of truth. The model-visible history is a
> deterministic projection. Request construction only produces the current
> request.

The result is a small agent that can survive compaction, window changes, and
process restarts without inventing history.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](quickstart.md) installs and runs the first task.
- [CLI](cli.md) lists one-shot, REPL, session, web, and recovery commands.
- [Configuration](configuration.md) documents `cade-mini.json`.
- [Architecture](architecture.md) explains the log, projection, request, and run
  pipeline.
- [Sessions and context](sessions-context.md) covers resume, compaction,
  pruning, and history retrieval.
- [Tools and security](tools-security.md) covers modes, rules, grants, and shell
  analysis.
- [Snapshots and goals](snapshots-goals.md) covers undo and durable objectives.
- [Skills and memory](skills-memory.md) covers `SKILL.md` and `MEMORY.md`.
- [Hooks, MCP, and subagents](hooks-mcp-subagents.md) covers extensions.
- [Hosts](hosts.md) covers the CLI REPL and the local web host.
- [Development](development.md) covers checks, tests, and the docs pipeline.
- [Parity](parity.md) links the acceptance against Cade.

## Built docs

The docs are Markdown-first. A small tool validates links and anchors, builds a
single-page site, and generates an `llms.txt` catalog for agents:

```bash
python -m cade_mini.docs check
python -m cade_mini.docs build
python -m cade_mini.docs llms --write
python -m cade_mini.docs catalogs --write
```

The generated site is [docs/index.html](../index.html); the generated
catalogs are `docs/cade-mini/llms.txt`, `docs/cade-mini/llms-full.txt`, and the
config, event, and module pages under `design/`.

# Quickstart

<!-- source: quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

Cade Mini requires Python 3.12 or newer. The repository uses `uv` for
development and for the `cade-mini` entry point.

## Install and authenticate

From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --locked
```

Cade Mini owns its credential store at `~/.cade-mini/auth.json`. Log in to
Codex with a browser or device code:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini login
uv run --locked cade-mini login --method device_code
```

For an API-key provider, use a hidden key prompt or set its environment variable:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini login --provider deepseek
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=...
uv run --locked cade-mini --provider deepseek --model deepseek-flash "Review this project."
```

The default provider is `openai-codex`. Set `provider` and `model` in
`cade-mini.json` to choose other startup defaults. Mini does not read Cade's
credentials, skills, or settings.

## Run one task

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini "Read README.md and explain the entry point in three bullets."
```

The same command can be written explicitly:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini exec "Read README.md and explain the entry point."
```

Cade Mini runs in the current directory by default. Use `--project-root` to
point at another workspace.

## Choose a mode

- `act` is the default. Reads run directly; writes and shell commands ask.
- `build` allows structured writes and read-only shell commands. Mutating shell
  commands still ask.
- `plan` hides write and edit tools and denies mutations. Read-only shell
  commands are allowed.

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --mode plan "Propose a fix for the failing test."
uv run --locked cade-mini --mode build "Fix the bug and run the test."
```

For non-interactive automation, `--yes` approves asks, and `--read-only` denies
writes and shell commands. Prefer rule-based allows over `--yes` for shared
repositories; see [Configuration](configuration.md).

## Continue work

Sessions live under `.cade-mini/sessions` by default.

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --list-sessions
uv run --locked cade-mini --continue "What did you change?"
uv run --locked cade-mini --resume SESSION_ID "Continue the task."
```

Omitting the task starts the interactive REPL. See [CLI](cli.md) for all REPL
commands.

## Open the web host

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --web --port 8765
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The web host has no terminal prompt, so writes and
shell commands are denied unless you start it with `--yes` or use rules. The
host serves one durable session for its lifetime.

## Build the docs

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs check
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs build
```

Open `docs/index.html`. The docs source is under `docs/cade-mini/`.

# CLI

<!-- source: cli.md -->

# CLI

The `cade-mini` entry point runs one task, starts a REPL, manages sessions, or
serves the web host.

```bash
cade-mini [TASK] [options]
cade-mini exec TASK [options]
```

`exec` is an explicit alias for a one-shot task. Without a task, `cade-mini`
starts the interactive REPL.

## Login

```bash
cade-mini login
cade-mini login --method device_code
cade-mini login --provider deepseek
```

`--provider` defaults to `openai-codex`. Codex supports `browser` (default) and
`device_code`; other providers use `api_key` with a hidden input prompt.
Credentials are stored in `~/.cade-mini/auth.json`. Login does not change
project provider or model settings.

## One-shot options

- `--project-root PATH` sets the workspace. The default is the current
  directory.
- `--config PATH` selects a config file. The default is
  `<project-root>/cade-mini.json`.
- `--provider NAME`, `--model NAME`, and `--effort EFFORT` override provider
  defaults.
- `--mode plan|build|act` selects the execution mode.
- `--read-only` / `--no-read-only` denies or permits writes and shell commands.
- `--yes` approves asks. Use it only in trusted, non-interactive contexts.
- `--auto-review` / `--no-auto-review` lets the model review ask-level calls.
- `--max-steps N` bounds model steps.
- `--context-window N` overrides the model context window.
- `--json` emits JSONL events for a one-shot task.
- `--steer TEXT` injects guidance at the next model step; repeatable.
- `--queue TEXT` queues a REPL task to run after the current task; repeatable.

## Sessions

- `--list-sessions` prints ID, update time, and title, then exits.
- `--continue` resumes the latest session in the project.
- `--resume` resumes the latest session; `--resume ID` resumes a specific one.
- `--sessions-dir PATH` changes the session directory. A relative path is
  resolved against the project root.
- `--undo` restores the latest file snapshot and exits without contacting a
  provider.

`--continue` and `--resume` cannot be combined.

## Goals and web host

- `--goal TEXT` sets the workspace goal before running.
- `--web` starts the local web host instead of the REPL.
- `--host` and `--port` bind the web host. The default is `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## REPL commands

- `/new` starts a new session.
- `/resume [ID]` resumes the latest or a specific session.
- `/sessions` lists project sessions.
- `/fork [N|ENTRY]` forks before a recent user turn or entry. `N=1` is the latest.
- `/clone` copies the current branch to a new session.
- `/tree` shows entries; `*` marks the active branch.
- `/rewind [N]` creates a session without the latest N user turns.
- `/compact` summarizes older turns.
- `/new-context [NOTE]` starts a new window, optionally with a handoff note.
- `/mode [MODE]` shows or switches the execution mode.
- `/permissions [clear]` shows or clears session grants.
- `/undo [N]` restores the latest N snapshots.
- `/goal [TEXT|done|clear]` shows, sets, completes, or clears the goal.
- `/context` prints the session ID, provider, budget, and event count.
- `/steer TEXT` queues guidance for the next model step.
- `/queue TEXT` queues a task to run after the current one.
- `/stop` cancels the current task at the next safe point.
- `/help` prints the command list.
- `/exit` or `/quit` exits.

## REPL input

- `@path` attaches a workspace file to the task.
- `$skill` loads a skill body into the task.
- `!command` runs a shell command without contacting the model. Permission
  checks still apply.

```text
Review @src/cade_mini/core/loop.py and use $review-only
!git status
```

During a task, the REPL keeps reading input:

- `/steer TEXT` appends guidance at the next model step.
- `/queue TEXT` runs TEXT after the current task.
- `/stop` cancels at the next safe point.
- Other text is queued as a follow-up task.

Steering is applied between steps, not inside a provider stream or a running
tool. See [Steering and queueing](design/steering-queue.md).

## Exit codes

- `0`: the run completed.
- `1`: the run ended without completion, or no snapshot was available for
  `--undo`.
- `2`: argument, configuration, or startup error.
- `130`: login was cancelled.

## Examples

```bash
cade-mini --list-sessions
cade-mini --continue "Summarize the current state."
cade-mini --undo
cade-mini --mode plan "Find the smallest fix for the failing test."
cade-mini --mode build --yes "Fix the test and run pytest."
cade-mini --web --port 8765
```

# Configuration

<!-- source: configuration.md -->

# Configuration

Cade Mini reads `<project-root>/cade-mini.json` by default. Use `--config PATH`
to select another file. Command-line options override the file; the file
overrides built-in defaults.

The file is strict: unknown keys and invalid values are rejected instead of
silently ignored.

## Example

```json
{
  "provider": "deepseek",
  "model": "deepseek-chat",
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "context_window": 128000,
  "max_steps": 30,
  "sessions_dir": ".cade-mini/sessions",
  "mode": "act",
  "read_only": false,
  "instructions": true,
  "note": true,
  "memory": true,
  "auto_review": false,
  "prompt_modules": ["identity", "tool_discipline", "working_note", "environment"],
  "rules": [
    {
      "tool": "bash",
      "command_prefix": "git status",
      "decision": "allow"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Fields

- `provider`, `model`: provider name and model identifier. The CLI flags
  override both.
- `reasoning_effort`: provider reasoning effort. The CLI flag is `--effort`.
- `context_window`: model context window in tokens.
- `max_steps`: maximum model steps in one run.
- `sessions_dir`: session directory. Relative paths resolve against the project
  root.
- `mode`: `plan`, `build`, or `act`.
- `read_only`: deny writes and shell commands.
- `instructions`: load `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` into request context.
- `note`: load `NOTE.md` working state.
- `memory`: load `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
- `auto_review`: let the model review ask-level tool calls. Default is false.
- `prompt_modules`: system prompt modules. Available names are `identity`,
  `tool_discipline`, `working_note`, and `environment`.

## Rules

Rules are evaluated last match first. A rule matches a tool name or `*`, and
optionally a path or command prefix. `decision` is `allow`, `deny`, or `ask`.

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git", "decision": "deny"},
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git status", "decision": "allow"},
    {"tool": "write", "path_prefix": "docs/", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

Hard boundaries win over rules: a path outside the workspace is denied even if a
rule allows the tool. `read_only` also wins over grants and rules.

## Hooks

Hooks run shell commands around tools. A non-zero `before_tool` hook denies the
call.

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "event": "before_tool",
      "command": "python tools/check_tool.py",
      "matcher": "bash",
      "timeout_ms": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```

`event` is `before_tool` or `after_tool`. `matcher` is a tool name, a prefix
ending in `*`, or omitted for all tools. Hooks receive `CADE_HOOK_EVENT`,
`CADE_TOOL_NAME`, `CADE_TOOL_ARGS`, and `CADE_TOOL_RESULT` in the environment.

## MCP servers

MCP servers use stdio and keep one persistent connection per server.

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["mcp_server.py"],
      "cwd": ".",
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "env": {"LOG_LEVEL": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

Discovered tools are exposed as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default,
are denied in plan mode and read-only mode, and can be allowed by a rule.

# Architecture

<!-- source: architecture.md -->

# Architecture

Cade Mini is a pipeline with four stages. Each stage has one owner and one
direction of data flow.

```text
Session log -> Conversation projection -> Request -> Run
```

## Session log

`SessionLog` is an append-only JSONL file. Each entry has an ID, timestamp,
type, parent ID, and data. The active branch ends at the latest entry. A tree is
possible, but the loop follows one branch.

The log stores facts:

- `system`, `user`, `assistant`, and `tool_result` are model-visible facts.
- `compaction` records a summary and `first_kept_id`.
- `window` records a new context start and an optional handoff.
- `request`, `run`, and `attempt` are audit facts. They never become
  conversation messages.

The schema is closed and versioned. See [Session log schema](../cade-mini-schema.md).

## Projection

`project(entries)` is a pure function. It reads the branch and produces the
deterministic conversation projection:

1. Take the latest system message.
2. Apply the latest window start.
3. Apply the latest compaction summary.
4. Keep retained user, assistant, and tool-result messages.
5. Pair tool calls with tool results; insert a synthetic interrupted result at
   the tail when the log ends mid-call.

No projection step writes to the log. Replaying the same entries always
produces the same conversation.

## Request

`build(conversation, tools, budget, context)` admits messages into the current
model window. It:

- joins request-only context such as instructions, skill catalog, NOTE, memory,
  and goal;
- replaces old tool bodies with references to the history tool;
- drops the oldest turns when needed;
- converts the result to provider wire format;
- returns a `Request` with a `BuildReport`.

Admission does not mutate the conversation and does not write facts. A request
that still exceeds the budget is rejected rather than silently truncated.

## Run

`run()` appends the user fact, calls the provider, appends assistant and
tool-result facts, and executes tools. It is the only stage that writes during a
turn. Compaction and window fallback are decisions expressed as new log facts.

## Package map

- `core/types.py`: log, message, block, and error types.
- `core/log.py`: append, lock, tail repair, session listing, copy/fork.
- `core/projection.py`: deterministic conversation projection.
- `core/request.py`: budget, admission, wire conversion.
- `core/loop.py`: provider stream, tool execution, retries, facts.
- `core/compaction.py` and `core/window.py`: context reduction decisions.
- `tools/workspace.py`, `tools/history.py`: workspace tools and evidence
  retrieval.
- `safety/policy.py`, `safety/shell.py`, `safety/grants.py`,
  `safety/approval.py`, `safety/review.py`: permissions and approvals.
- `extensions/skills.py`, `extensions/memory.py`, `extensions/hooks.py`,
  `extensions/mcp.py`, `extensions/subagents.py`, `extensions/snapshots.py`,
  `extensions/goal.py`: add-ons and durable host state.
- `app/config.py`, `app/provider.py`, `app/auth.py`, `app/prompts.py`,
  `app/instructions.py`, `app/note.py`: startup and request context.
- `hosts/cli.py`, `hosts/web.py`, `docs.py`: hosts and documentation.

Mini owns `cade_mini.ai` and `cade_mini.execution_env` as lower layers for
provider protocols and local process execution. It does not depend on the
separate Cade project. `test_mini_boundary.py` rejects old Cade imports and
application dependencies in these lower layers. There are no top-level
re-exports; import the owning submodule directly.

## Why the split

The split prevents a common failure: the request builder starts hiding
messages, then the history rewrite becomes the only copy of what happened. Mini
keeps the original facts and lets the projection and admission be replaced
without losing history.

# Sessions and context

<!-- source: sessions-context.md -->

# Sessions and context

A session is an append-only JSONL file under `.cade-mini/sessions` by default.
The file name is `session-<id>.jsonl`. The session title is derived from the
first user message; no extra event type is needed.

## Resume

```bash
cade-mini --list-sessions
cade-mini --continue "Continue where we stopped."
cade-mini --resume SESSION_ID "Explain the current state."
```

`--continue` and `--resume` open the latest or a specific session. Existing
sessions keep their original system fact; a new `cade-mini.json` does not rewrite
history. If a resumed session has no system entry, the current prompt is added.

## Fork, clone, tree, and rewind

- `/clone` copies the active branch into a new session.
- `/fork [N|ENTRY]` copies history before a user turn (default: latest) into a
  new session and prints the forked input.
- `/tree` lists entries; `*` marks the active branch.
- `/rewind [N]` creates a new session without the latest N user turns.
- `/undo [N]` restores the latest N file snapshots.

These operations create new sessions; they do not rewrite the original file.
Compaction and window references are remapped when entries are copied.

## Compaction

When the full conversation exceeds the input budget, `Compactor`:

1. Selects a cut at a visible user boundary.
2. Sends the older messages to the provider for a summary.
3. Appends a `compaction` fact with the summary and `first_kept_id`.
4. Reprojects the conversation as the latest system, summary, and retained tail.

Compaction is iterative: a prior summary is serialized as `PRIOR SUMMARY` and
can be summarized again. The original user, assistant, and tool-result facts
remain in the log.

## Pruning

Request admission replaces old tool results with a reference:

```text
[tool output omitted; call_id=...; use the history tool ...]
```

The latest four tool results are protected first. If the request still does not
fit, older protected results and finally the newest result can be replaced. The
model can recover exact content with the `history` tool using `call_id` or
`entry_id`.

## Windows

A `window` fact starts a new context at a user entry and may include a handoff.
The CLI can start one explicitly with `/new-context`. If compaction cannot bring
a request under budget, the loop can append an automatic window with a fixed
handoff that points to `NOTE.md` and the history tool.

## History tool

`history` accepts one of:

- `query`: case-insensitive search over the branch, returning entry IDs and
  snippets.
- `entry_id`: exact content of one log entry.
- `call_id`: exact tool result for one call.

Exact content is capped. Search results are capped and point back to entry IDs.

## Request context order

For each task the request contains:

1. The system message.
2. Project instructions from `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or their variants.
3. The skill catalog.
4. `NOTE.md` working state.
5. `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
6. An active goal.

Items 2-6 are request-only context. They are recorded in the request audit but
never become conversation facts. See [Architecture](architecture.md) and the
[design](../cade-mini.md).

# How Cade Mini works

<!-- source: design/how-it-works.md -->

# How Cade Mini works

Cade Mini coordinates one model request at a time, executes the requested tools,
and records every durable fact in a session log.

## One run

A submitted task is appended as a `user` fact. Cade Mini projects the active
branch, builds a request for the current budget, and sends it to the provider.
The provider streams text and tool calls. The loop records the assistant
message, executes each tool call, and records a tool result. If the model needs
another request, the loop starts another step; otherwise the run ends.

A step is one request plus the tools caused by its response. A run can contain
many steps. The loop stops on completion, a step limit, context exhaustion,
cancellation, or a provider error.

## Context

The projection supplies conversation history. Request-only context supplies
project instructions, the skill catalog, `NOTE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and an active
goal. Tool results are pruned when they no longer fit; the history tool can read
the original facts.

Compaction adds a summary fact and keeps a recent tail. A window moves the
context start forward and may include a handoff. Neither operation rewrites the
original messages.

## Sessions

Sessions are JSONL files under `.cade-mini/sessions`. Entries have IDs and parent
IDs, so a session can form a tree; the active branch ends at the latest entry.
Resuming opens the same file and appends new facts.

## Interfaces

The terminal host runs one task or a REPL. The web host serves a page and a
small JSON API. Both call the same loop and share policy, tools, and session
storage.

## Extensions

Skills add on-demand instructions. Memory adds durable facts. Hooks run shell
commands around tools. MCP adds remote tools. Subagents run an independent child
session. Each extension is a narrow adapter over the loop, not a change to the
session schema.

## Trust and permissions

Every tool call passes through a policy. Modes, static rules, session grants,
shell classification, and approvals decide whether a call runs. Cade Mini has
no OS sandbox; the path boundary, mode, shell classification, and approvals are
the active safety layer.

See [Architecture](../architecture.md) for the invariant and
[Capability seams](capability-seams.md) for the contracts.

# Code map

<!-- source: design/code-map.md -->

# Code map

Cade Mini is an independent project. The `cade-mini` distribution installs the
`cade_mini` package and the `cade-mini` command. It does not install or depend
on Cade.

## Package layout

```text
src/cade_mini/
  ai/             provider adapters, events, auth protocols, models
  execution_env/  local subprocess execution and output capture
  core/           log, projection, request, loop, compaction, window
  tools/          workspace actions and history retrieval
  safety/         policy, shell analysis, grants, approval, review
  extensions/     skills, memory, hooks, mcp, subagents, snapshots, goal
  app/            config, provider assembly, credentials, request context
  hosts/          cli, auth, web
  docs.py
  __main__.py
tests/            regression and integration tests
```

Provider and execution modules originated in Cade and are now owned and
maintained here. Mini includes only the process execution code it uses, not
Cade's filesystem or Linux sandbox implementation. Mini has no OS sandbox.

## Entry points

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini
uv run --locked cade-mini exec "Fix the failing test."
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini
uv run --locked cade-mini login
uv run --locked cade-mini --web --port 8765
```

The console script and Python module call `cade_mini.hosts.cli:main`. Login
is handled by `cade_mini.hosts.auth`. Credentials and user skills live under
`~/.cade-mini/`. Project sessions and other state live under `.cade-mini/`.
No old Cade directories or commands are used.

## Import direction

- `ai` and `execution_env` do not import application or host modules.
- `core` imports core types and AI protocols.
- `tools`, `safety`, and `extensions` connect actions and policies to the core.
- `app` owns startup settings, credential persistence, and request context.
- `hosts` assemble these components and own user interaction.

`tests/test_mini_boundary.py` rejects imports from the old `cade` namespace
and application imports in the lower layers. The package root has no public
re-exports; import the owning submodule directly.

See [Architecture](../architecture.md),
[How Cade Mini works](how-it-works.md), and
[Capability seams](capability-seams.md) for runtime contracts.

# Relationship to Cade

<!-- source: design/cade-comparison.md -->

# Relationship to Cade

Cade and Cade Mini are separate projects. This repository develops, tests, and
releases only Cade Mini. It does not provide compatibility with Cade's Python
package, commands, settings, credentials, or session formats.

Mini originated as a log-first implementation alongside Cade. Its provider
adapters and process execution code were brought into the `cade_mini` package
when it became independent. They are no longer shared runtime dependencies.

## Mini's product boundary

Mini provides a terminal REPL, one-shot execution, and a local web host. Its
core separates append-only session facts, deterministic projection, request
admission, and the run loop.

Intentional limits include:

- No full-screen TUI, plugin runtime, RPC, or SDK.
- No artifact store or parallel tool scheduler.
- No permanent approval grants; durable rules belong in project config.
- No OS sandbox; permissions and shell classification are application checks.

The [historical parity acceptance](../parity.md) records workflows tested
before separation. It is not a promise of future feature parity. See the
[code map](code-map.md) for the current package and ownership boundaries.

# Capability seams

<!-- source: design/capability-seams.md -->

# Capability seams

Cade Mini keeps a small number of explicit contracts. A seam is a place where an
implementation can be replaced without changing the session schema or the loop.

| Seam | Contract | Implementations | Main consumers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | `loop.Provider` streaming events | Chat providers, Codex | Loop, compaction, auto-review |
| Tool | `loop.Tool` name, description, parameters, execute | Workspace tools, history, skill, memory, goal, subagent, MCP | Loop |
| Policy | `loop.Policy.check` returns allow, deny, or ask | `WorkspacePolicy` | Loop |
| Approval | Callable returning bool or awaitable bool | `SessionApprover`, `AutoReviewer` | Loop |
| Hooks | `loop.Hooks.before/after` | `HookRunner` | Loop |
| Compaction | `Compactor(log, budget)` | LLM summary compactor | Loop |
| Session store | `SessionLog` append, branch, open | File-backed JSONL log | Every layer above it |
| Recovery | `SnapshotStore` capture and undo | File snapshot store | Tools, CLI |
| Host | A task runner over the loop | CLI, web host | Users |

## Provider

The loop needs a streaming event source: text deltas, tool calls, a final
message, usage, and failures. A provider owns wire conversion and replay state.
Cade Mini does not depend on provider-specific message types above this seam.

## Tool

A tool declares a JSON schema and an async `execute`. A tool result is content,
an error flag, and optional metadata. Tools do not write the session log; the
loop records their results.

## Policy and approval

Policy returns a decision, not an execution. Approval is only consulted for
`ask`. A denial becomes a tool error fact, so the model can recover. Keeping
these separate lets the host choose a TTY prompt, a model reviewer, or a
non-interactive denial.

## Hooks

Hooks observe and can veto a tool call without changing the policy result. A
`before_tool` failure is a denial; `after_tool` failure is ignored. Hooks are
trusted configuration, not sandboxed code.

## Stores

`SessionLog` is the durable history. `SnapshotStore`, `GoalStore`, and the
memory and NOTE files are host state, not session facts. Treating them as
separate stores keeps the schema closed while allowing recovery and long-term
state.

## Host

A host owns presentation, input, and the event loop boundary. It does not own
the agent loop or the schema. The CLI and web host differ only in how they run a
task and render events.

## Tests as contracts

Each seam has a focused test module. `test_mini_boundary.py` enforces the import
firewall, so a seam cannot quietly become a dependency on the Cade product
layers.

# Event model

<!-- source: design/event-model.md -->

# Event model

A session is a tree of entries, not a message array. Entry types fall into two
groups.

## Model-visible facts

These entries project into the conversation:

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Base system prompt; the latest one wins |
| `user` | User task or steering input |
| `assistant` | Text and tool calls produced by one model response |
| `tool_result` | Result paired to a tool call |
| `compaction` | Summary plus `first_kept_id`; shadows older entries |
| `window` | New context start plus optional handoff |

`compaction` and `window` also carry projections of their own: a summary
message. The original entries remain readable by the history tool.

## Audit facts

These entries never project:

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `meta` | Session creation metadata |
| `request` | Provider, model, context, digests, estimated tokens, dropped evidence |
| `attempt` | One provider attempt, including failures and retries |
| `run` | Termination, steps, usage, error |

Audit facts make the request reproducible without turning diagnostics into
conversation. A failed run therefore cannot fabricate an assistant message.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  log[Session log] --> project[Projection]
  project --> conversation[Conversation]
  conversation --> request[Request build]
  request --> provider[Provider stream]
  provider --> facts[Assistant and tool-result facts]
  facts --> log
  request --> audit[request fact]
  provider --> attempts[attempt facts]
  facts --> run[run fact]
```

The loop appends the user fact before the first request. Each step appends one
assistant fact and zero or more tool-result facts. A run appends exactly one
`run` fact.

## Ordering and pairing

A tool result follows its assistant tool call. Projection rejects an orphan
result or a duplicate result. If the branch ends after a tool call without a
result, projection inserts a synthetic interrupted result at the tail so the
request remains protocol-valid.

## Compaction and windows

A compaction cuts at a user boundary. Its summary message appears first in the
retained context. A window discards earlier entries and may insert a handoff.
Only the latest cut applies. Compaction is preferred; a window is a fallback
when a summary cannot fit.

## Schema authority

The closed schema is in [Session log schema](../../cade-mini-schema.md). The
generated [event catalog](event-catalog.md) lists the current event types from
code.

# Tool execution

<!-- source: design/tool-execution.md -->

# Tool execution

Every tool call follows the same pipeline. Policy and approval decide whether a
call may run; hooks can stop it; the loop owns execution and recording.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  call[Tool call] --> policy[Policy decision]
  policy -->|deny| denied[Denied tool result]
  policy -->|ask| approval[Approval]
  approval -->|deny| denied
  approval -->|allow| before[before_tool hooks]
  policy -->|allow| before
  before -->|deny| hookdenied[Hook-denied result]
  before -->|allow| execute[Execute tool]
  execute --> after[after_tool hooks]
  execute --> result[Tool result]
  result --> log[Append fact]
  denied --> log
  hookdenied --> log
```

## Order

1. The model returns a tool call with an ID and arguments.
2. Policy checks tool name, path, mode, rules, grants, and shell classification.
3. An `ask` decision is resolved by the host: TTY prompt, `--yes`, auto-review,
   or denial.
4. `before_tool` hooks run. A non-zero exit denies the call.
5. The tool executes with a timeout and cancellation token.
6. The result is truncated, appended as a `tool_result` fact, and rendered.
7. `after_tool` hooks run and their output is ignored.

## Denials and errors

A denied call is not an exception. It becomes an error tool result so the model
can adapt. Unknown tools, malformed arguments, timeouts, and thrown exceptions
also become error results. A cancellation appends interrupted results for any
remaining calls before the run terminates.

## Hooks

Hooks receive the tool name, JSON arguments, and the result for `after_tool`.
They run with the workspace as the current directory. A hook timeout is a
denial or a silently ignored observer, never an unbounded wait.

## Evidence retention

Tool results are facts. Request admission can replace old bodies with a
reference that names the `call_id`. The history tool retrieves the exact result
from the branch, so pruning does not destroy evidence.

## Tests

- `test_mini_loop.py` covers approval, errors, timeouts, cancellation, retries,
  and window fallback.
- `test_mini_hooks.py` covers allow, deny, and after-hook execution.
- `test_mini_policy.py` covers modes, rules, grants, and boundaries.

See [Tools and security](../tools-security.md) for user-facing behavior.
