# Tool catalog

<!-- source: design/tool-catalog.md -->

# Tool catalog

The built-in tool surface. MCP tools are discovered at startup and named
`mcp__<server>__<tool>`; their parameters come from the server.

| Tool | Parameters | Side effect | Default policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | `path`, `offset`, `limit` | None | Allow inside workspace |
| `write` | `path`, `content` | Creates or replaces a file; snapshot first | Ask in act, allow in build |
| `edit` | `path`, `old`, `new` | Replaces one occurrence; snapshot first | Ask in act, allow in build |
| `glob` | `pattern`, `path` | None | Allow |
| `grep` | `pattern`, `path`, `include` | None | Allow |
| `bash` | `command`, `workdir`, `timeout_ms` | Arbitrary process; snapshot common mutations | Ask except read-only shell |
| `history` | `query`, `entry_id`, `call_id`, `limit` | None | Allow |
| `skill` | `name` | None; loads a skill body | Allow |
| `memory` | `text` | Appends to `MEMORY.md` | Allow; denied read-only |
| `goal` | `action`, `objective` | Updates `.cade-mini/goal.json` | Allow |
| `subagent` | `prompt`, `description` | Creates a child session | Allow; hidden in plan |
| `delegate` | `prompt` or `tasks`, `mode`, `description` | Creates one or more child sessions | Allow |
| `mcp__*` | Server-defined | Remote side effects | Ask; denied plan and read-only |

## Reading the table

- "Side effect" is what the tool can change, not what it always changes.
- `write` and `edit` fail closed if the snapshot cannot be taken.
- `bash` read-only classification is conservative; unknown commands ask in
  build and act and are denied in plan.
- MCP tools are dynamic. A rule can allow a specific tool; the default is ask.

## Parameters

The authoritative JSON schemas are built into each tool. This table is a
navigation aid; when it disagrees with the tool schema, the schema wins.

## Related

- [Tools and security](../tools-security.md)
- [Tool execution](../design/tool-execution.md)
- [Configuration catalog](config-catalog.md)

# MCP reference servers

<!-- source: design/mcp-reference.md -->

# MCP reference servers

Cade Mini implements stdio `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` with a
persistent connection per server. That is enough for the reference servers that
expose tools.

## Verified servers

| Server | Command | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filesystem | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <dir>` | Discovery and `read_text_file` |
| Memory | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` | Discovery of entity tools |
| Sequential Thinking | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking` | Discovery of `sequentialthinking` |
| Time | `uvx mcp-server-time` | Discovery and `get_current_time` |
| Fetch | `uvx mcp-server-fetch` | Server starts and lists tools |

On Windows, run npm servers through `cmd /c`:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "time": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-time"]
    },
    "fs": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": [
        "/c", "npx", "-y",
        "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem",
        "C:/path/to/workspace"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

On POSIX use `npx` directly. The Git server needs its repository flag, for
example `--repository <path>`; pass the exact arguments the server expects.

## Capability boundary

The reference servers above are tool servers. Cade Mini does not implement MCP
resources, prompts, sampling, or server-initiated requests. A server that relies
on those features will start but expose only its tools.

## Policy

MCP tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default, are denied in
plan mode and with `--read-only`, and can be allowed by a rule:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "mcp__time__get_current_time", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

## Verify

```bash
cade-mini --mode build "Use the time MCP tool to get the current time in Asia/Singapore."
```

The log records a `tool_result` with the server's text content. A server process
is closed when Cade Mini exits.

## Related

- [Configuration](../configuration.md)
- [Hooks, MCP, and subagents](../hooks-mcp-subagents.md)
- [Custom MCP server](../cookbook/custom-mcp.md)

# Steering and queueing

<!-- source: design/steering-queue.md -->

# Steering and queueing

Cade Mini's REPL can read input while a task is running. The host does not block
the terminal on `_run_task`.

## Why the old REPL blocked

The first REPL called `input()` in the main thread and then ran the async loop
with `asyncio.run`. While that call was active, the terminal was not read, so
`/steer` and `/queue` could only affect the next task.

## Current design

```text
stdin
  |
  v
_InputPump thread  -- _Line -->  event queue
                                  |
task thread  -- _ApprovalRequest / _TaskDone --> event queue
                                  |
                                  v
                         REPL main thread
```

- `_InputPump` reads one line at a time and never calls the model.
- `_run_task` runs in a worker thread with its own `asyncio` event loop.
- The REPL main thread owns the event queue and the session state.
- `_HostApprover` sends `_ApprovalRequest` to the main thread and waits. The
  main thread reads the answer from the same input pump, so approvals do not
  compete with a second `input()`.
- `!command` runs in the main thread and uses `_ConsoleApprover`, which reads
  the answer directly from the event queue.

## Commands during a run

| Input | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/steer TEXT` | Append guidance at the next model step |
| `/queue TEXT` | Run TEXT as a new task after the current task |
| `/stop` or `/cancel` | Cancel the current task at the next safe point |
| other text | Same as `/queue`: run it after the current task |
| `/exit` | Cancel, wait for the task to settle, then exit |

`/steer` is not a prompt injection into a running provider request. The loop
checks the steering queue before each step, appends a `user` fact with
`source: runtime`, and builds the next request from the projection. This keeps
the session log as the source of truth.

## Queue semantics

- A queued task starts automatically when the current task reaches a terminal
  state.
- Queue order is FIFO.
- A queued task runs in the same session; it is not a fork.
- `/fork`, `/clone`, `/rewind`, and session commands are main-thread commands.
  They are only handled when no task is active. During a run they are treated as
  queued text; finish or stop the run first.

## Limits

- Tools already executing are not killed. `/stop` takes effect at the next
  cancellation check.
- The input pump uses plain `input()`, not a full line editor. Editing,
  history, and completion are terminal features.
- Approval answers are read as the next line. Do not type a task while an
  approval prompt is waiting; it is consumed as the answer.
- The one-shot `--steer` flag seeds guidance before the first step. It is not a
  substitute for `/steer` during a run.

## Tests

- `test_live_input_handles_steer_and_queue`
- `test_live_input_is_read_while_worker_is_running`
- `test_mid_run_steer_reaches_the_next_provider_request`
- `test_repl_reads_steer_while_a_bash_tool_is_running`
- `test_host_approver_routes_through_events`
- `test_live_input_can_stop_the_task`

The end-to-end test blocks a tool until the host delivers `/steer`, then checks
that the next provider request contains the steering fact.

# Persistence catalog

<!-- source: design/persistence-catalog.md -->

# Persistence catalog

Cade Mini separates durable history from host state. The session log is the
authority for what the model saw and what happened; the other stores have
narrower jobs.

| Artifact | Default location | Owner | Lifetime | Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session log | `.cade-mini/sessions/session-*.jsonl` | `SessionLog` | Project | Closed v1 |
| Snapshots | `.cade-mini/snapshots/` | `SnapshotStore` | Project | Local index |
| Goal | `.cade-mini/goal.json` | `GoalStore` | Project | One object |
| Working note | `NOTE.md` | Project | Project | Markdown |
| Memory | `MEMORY.md` | `MemoryTool` | Project | Markdown |
| Instructions | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, overrides | Project | Project | Markdown |
| Skills | `~/.cade-mini/skills`, `.cade-mini/skills` | Discovery | User or project | `SKILL.md` |
| Config | `cade-mini.json` | `MiniConfig` | Project | Pydantic, strict |
| Credentials | `~/.cade-mini/auth.json` | `JsonCredentialStore` | User | Provider credentials |
| Docs site | `docs/index.html` | Docs tool | Repository | Generated |
| LLM catalogs | `docs/cade-mini/llms*.txt` | Docs tool | Repository | Generated |

## The session log

The log is append-only and versioned. It stores model-visible facts and audit
facts in one tree. It is the only artifact needed to reconstruct the
conversation. Compaction and windows are log entries, not rewrites.

## Snapshots

Snapshots are an undo journal for file changes. They cover `write`, `edit`, and
common single-command shell mutations. The index is JSONL and each snapshot has
a metadata file plus an optional payload. They are not part of the session
branch.

## Goals and notes

A goal is one objective with an active or done status. `NOTE.md` is working
state that is included in every request and summarized during compaction.
`MEMORY.md` is durable project knowledge. These files are intentionally plain:
they can be edited by hand and inspected with ordinary tools.

## Generated artifacts

The docs site, `llms.txt`, and `llms-full.txt` are generated from Markdown and
`docs.json`. They are checked for freshness; do not edit the HTML by hand.

## What is not persisted

- Request-only context is recorded in the request audit, not as messages.
- Grants last for the process; durable policy belongs in config rules.
- Approval prompts and TUI state are host state.
- Provider replay payloads live inside the assistant fact that produced them.

See [Session log schema](../../cade-mini-schema.md) for field-level detail and
[Change policy](../persistence/change-policy.md) for schema changes.

# Glossary

<!-- source: design/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

One canonical term per concept. Links point to the owning page.

## session log

The append-only JSONL file that records facts. It is the source of truth for the
active branch. See [Log](../subsystems/log.md).

## branch

A path through the entry tree. The active branch ends at the latest entry and
supplies the projection.

## projection

The deterministic conversation produced from a branch. It applies the latest
system, compaction, and window cuts, then pairs tool calls with results. See
[Projection and request](../subsystems/projection-request.md).

## request

The admitted, provider-ready form of a conversation for one model call. It
includes tools, budget, and request-only context. A request is not a fact and is
never projected.

## run

One invocation of the loop over a task. A run contains one or more steps and
ends with a `run` fact.

## step

One model request plus the tool calls caused by its response.

## tool result

The recorded output of one tool call, paired by call ID. It is a fact.

## compaction

A fact that adds a summary and a `first_kept_id`. It shadows older messages in
later projections without deleting them.

## window

A fact that moves the context start forward, optionally with a handoff. It is a
fallback when compaction cannot fit.

## history

The tool that retrieves exact evidence by entry ID or call ID after compaction
or pruning.

## mode

`plan`, `build`, or `act`. A mode selects the default policy for tools and shell
commands.

## rule

A static policy entry in config. Rules can match tool, path prefix, and command
prefix and return allow, deny, or ask.

## grant

A process-local approval created by answering `a`. It matches the same tool and
path or command.

## hook

A configured shell command around a tool call (`before_tool` or `after_tool`).

## skill

A `SKILL.md` body loaded on demand. The request carries a catalog; the `skill`
tool loads the body.

## MCP

Model Context Protocol. Cade Mini runs stdio MCP servers and exposes their tools
as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

## subagent

A child run with its own session and a restricted tool set. It cannot spawn
another subagent.

## snapshot

A pre-change copy of a file, used by `--undo` and `/undo`.

## goal

A durable objective in `.cade-mini/goal.json`, separate from the session
schema.

# Testing

<!-- source: design/testing.md -->

# Testing

Tests are grouped by the layer they protect. Run the smallest group that covers
a change, then the full suite before a release.

## Commands

```bash
mkdir -p e2e-results
uv run --locked pytest -q tests --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
uv run --locked pytest -q tests/test_mini_loop.py --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
uv run --locked ruff check src/cade_mini/ tests/
uv run --locked ruff format --check src/cade_mini/ tests/
uv run --locked pyright src/cade_mini/
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs check
```

## Coverage map

| Area | Tests |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | `test_mini_log.py` |
| Projection and pairing | `test_mini_projection.py` |
| Budget, pruning, wire format | `test_mini_request.py` |
| Loop, approvals, retries, windows | `test_mini_loop.py` |
| Provider and auth | `test_mini_provider.py`, `test_mini_auth.py`, `test_responses_codex_cache_contract.py` |
| Workspace tools | `test_mini_tools.py` |
| Compaction and windows | `test_mini_compaction.py`, `test_mini_window.py` |
| CLI and config | `test_mini_cli.py`, `test_mini_config.py` |
| Instructions, skills, memory, NOTE | `test_mini_instructions.py`, `test_mini_skills.py`, `test_mini_memory.py`, `test_mini_note.py` |
| Safety and modes | `test_mini_policy.py`, `test_mini_shell.py`, `test_mini_grants.py` |
| Extensions | `test_mini_hooks.py`, `test_mini_mcp.py`, `test_mini_subagents.py` |
| Recovery | `test_mini_snapshots.py`, `test_mini_goal.py` |
| Hosts | `test_mini_web.py` |
| Docs | `test_mini_docs.py` |
| Import firewall | `test_mini_boundary.py` |

## Real-provider checks

The acceptance runs use DeepSeek or Codex and are not part of the default test
suite. They cover tool use, resume, compaction, skills, build mode, the web
host, and Codex write/read. Record the command and observed result in the change
that adds a new acceptance.

## Docs checks

`test_mini_docs.py` and `python -m cade_mini.docs check` validate the manifest,
links, anchors, and generated catalogs. The docs job runs in CI.

## Standalone distribution

Build the wheel and source archive with `uv build --no-sources`. Install the
wheel in a clean virtual environment and check both `cade-mini --help` and
`python -m cade_mini --help` outside the source tree. No Cade package or command
should be present. See the [validation guidelines](../../testing.md).

# Subsystems

<!-- source: subsystems/README.md -->

# Subsystems

Each page owns one subsystem's types, behavior, and failure modes. The
[architecture](../architecture.md) is the map; these pages are the reference.

- [Log](log.md): append, lock, branch, list, and repair.
- [Projection and request](projection-request.md): deterministic context and
  budget admission.
- [Loop](loop.md): provider calls, tools, approvals, retries, and facts.
- [Tools and policy](tools-policy.md): workspace tools, modes, rules, grants,
  shell classification, approvals.
- [Context and compaction](context-compaction.md): summaries, windows, history,
  and request context.
- [Extensions](extensions.md): skills, memory, hooks, MCP, subagents, snapshots,
  goals, and hosts.

A subsystem page describes current behavior. Historical decisions belong in
[decision records](../decisions/README.md) and incidents in
[postmortems](../postmortem/README.md).

# Log

<!-- source: subsystems/log.md -->

# Log

`SessionLog` owns the append-only JSONL file.

## Create and open

- `SessionLog.create(directory, session_id=None)` creates a unique file and
  writes a `meta` entry.
- `SessionLog.open(path)` validates the file and repairs a torn final line by
  appending a newline or dropping the incomplete tail.
- The session ID is derived from the file name when not supplied.

## Append

`append(type, data)`:

1. Takes an exclusive file lock.
2. Reads the current tail to get the parent ID.
3. Builds an entry with ID, timestamp, parent, type, and data.
4. Appends one JSON line and flushes.
5. Releases the lock.

`fsync` is deliberate: a returned append is durable enough to resume. A failed
write raises `LogError` and does not return a fake entry.

## Branch

`branch()` follows parent IDs from the last entry back to the root and reverses
the list. It rejects cycles, missing parents, and duplicate IDs.

## Listing and titles

`list_sessions(directory)` returns session ID, update time, and a title derived
from the first user text. Corrupt files are skipped so one bad session cannot
break the list.

## Invariants

- Entries are never rewritten in place.
- IDs are unique within a file.
- A parent precedes its child.
- The file ends with exactly one newline.
- The schema version is closed; new event types require a decision record.

## Tests

`test_mini_log.py` covers create, append, resume, tail repair, branching, and
listing. `test_mini_projection.py` covers malformed branches.

# Projection and request

<!-- source: subsystems/projection-request.md -->

# Projection and request

## Projection

`project(entries)` is pure. It:

1. Finds the latest `system` entry.
2. Applies the latest `window` start.
3. Applies the latest `compaction` cut and emits a summary message.
4. Converts user, assistant, and tool-result facts to messages.
5. Pairs each tool call with its result by call ID.
6. Inserts a synthetic interrupted result if the branch ends inside a call.

It rejects orphan results, duplicate results, and cuts that do not point to a
user entry. The projection does not call a provider or write the log.

## Request

`build(conversation, tools, budget, context)`:

1. Joins the base system prompt with request-only context.
2. Estimates tokens.
3. Replaces old tool bodies with references, keeping recent results first.
4. Drops the oldest user turns if still over budget.
5. Converts to provider messages and tool definitions.
6. Returns a `Request` and a `BuildReport`.

`BuildReport` records estimated tokens, budget, dropped call IDs, and dropped
turns. A request that cannot fit raises `RequestTooLarge`.

## Pruning rules

- The latest four tool results are protected in the first pass.
- If still over, protected results are pruned oldest first.
- The newest result is pruned only as a last resort.
- The replacement names the call ID and points to the history tool.

## Context order

The system message carries base instructions plus, in order: instructions,
skill catalog, NOTE, memory, and goal. These inputs are request-only; the
request audit records their digests and lengths, not their full text.

## Tests

`test_mini_projection.py`, `test_mini_request.py`, and
`test_mini_compaction.py` cover the cut, pruning, and wire-format contracts.

# Loop

<!-- source: subsystems/loop.md -->

# Loop

`run(log, text, ...)` is the only stage that writes during a turn.

## One run

1. Append the `user` fact.
2. For each step:
   - Project the branch.
   - If the full estimate exceeds budget, call the compactor.
   - Build the request.
   - If still over, call the window fallback.
   - Append a `request` audit fact.
   - Stream the provider.
   - Append the assistant fact.
   - Resolve and execute each tool call.
   - Append tool-result facts.
3. Append one `run` fact with termination, steps, usage, and error.

## Provider handling

The loop collects text deltas, tool calls, usage, and provider replay state. A
failure becomes an `attempt` fact. Retryable failures are retried once by
default; the retry delay is configurable. A terminal failure ends the run with
`provider_error` and never creates an assistant fact.

## Termination

- `completed`: the provider ended without tool calls.
- `step_limit`: the configured step count was reached.
- `context_error`: no request fits after compaction and window fallback.
- `aborted`: cancellation was requested.
- `provider_error`: the provider failed.

## Cancellation

A cancellation token is checked between steps and tool calls. Running tools get
the token; remaining calls receive interrupted results. The run records the
reason in its `run` fact.

## Events

The host receives text deltas, tool start, tool end, and final output. Events are
presentation; facts are durable. A host can drop events without losing history.

## Tests

`test_mini_loop.py` covers completion, tool use, approvals, retries, timeouts,
cancellation, context errors, and window fallback.

# Tools and policy

<!-- source: subsystems/tools-policy.md -->

# Tools and policy

## Tool contract

A tool has a name, description, JSON parameter schema, and async execute. Results
carry content, an error flag, and optional metadata. The loop records results; a
tool never appends to the log.

## Built-in tools

- Workspace: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `bash`.
- Evidence and context: `history`, `skill`, `memory`, `goal`.
- Delegation: `subagent`.
- Remote: `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

`write` and `edit` snapshot the target before changing it. `bash` snapshots
common single-command mutation targets.

## Policy

`WorkspacePolicy.check` returns allow, deny, or ask.

Hard checks run first:

- `read` and file writes must stay inside the workspace.
- `bash` workdir must stay inside the workspace.
- Unknown tools are denied.
- `read_only` denies writes, edits, shell, memory, and MCP.

Then:

1. A matching static rule decides.
2. A matching session grant allows.
3. The mode default decides.

Modes:

- `plan`: read tools and read-only shell; writes and mutations denied.
- `build`: writes allowed; read-only shell allowed; mutating shell asks.
- `act`: writes and shell ask.

## Shell classification

`classify_command` labels a command read-only, mutating, or unknown. Pipelines,
redirections, command lists, substitutions, and unknown binaries are unknown.
Plan mode denies unknown; build asks; act asks.

## Grants

`GrantStore` records a path or command for the exact tool. A grant is
process-local. `/permissions` lists and clears it. Durable policy belongs in
rules.

## Approvals

The host resolves ask. `SessionApprover` prompts a TTY with yes/no/always.
`AutoReviewer` makes one tool-free model call and requires an `ALLOW` prefix.
Non-interactive hosts deny unless `--yes` or a rule allows.

## Process isolation

There is no OS sandbox. Shell commands run with the Cade Mini process
permissions. The path boundary, mode, shell classification, and approvals are
the safety layer.

## Tests

`test_mini_tools.py`, `test_mini_policy.py`, `test_mini_grants.py`, and
`test_mini_shell.py`.

# Context and compaction

<!-- source: subsystems/context-compaction.md -->

# Context and compaction

## Request context

The system message is the base prompt plus request-only context:

1. Project instructions from `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or variants.
2. Skill catalog names and descriptions.
3. `NOTE.md` working state.
4. `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
5. An active goal.

The request audit records this context's digests; it does not turn the text into
conversation messages.

## Compaction

`Compactor` runs when the full projection exceeds the input budget.

1. Select the cut at a user boundary that keeps the recent tail under the
   configured target.
2. Serialize older messages, including a prior summary.
3. Ask the provider for a summary with a bounded output.
4. Append a `compaction` fact with summary and `first_kept_id`.
5. Reproject.

A summary failure or a cut with no messages appends an `attempt` fact and leaves
the conversation unchanged. A prior summary is included as `PRIOR SUMMARY`, so
compaction is iterative.

## Window fallback

If compaction cannot fit, the loop may call the window hook. The CLI starts a
window at the latest user entry with a fixed handoff that points to `NOTE.md`
and history. If the request still does not fit, the run terminates with
`context_error`.

## History

The `history` tool searches the branch or reads an exact entry or tool result.
It is the recovery path for evidence replaced during pruning or compaction.
Exact content is capped; search results point to entry IDs.

## Request pruning

Admission replaces old tool bodies with references before it drops turns. The
history tool remains the only exact source. See
[Projection and request](projection-request.md).

## Tests

`test_mini_compaction.py`, `test_mini_window.py`, `test_mini_history.py`, and
the request tests cover cuts, summaries, fallback, and retrieval.

# Extensions

<!-- source: subsystems/extensions.md -->

# Extensions

Extensions add behavior through narrow seams. None changes the session schema.

## Skills

Discovery reads `SKILL.md` from user and project roots. The request carries a
catalog; the `skill` tool loads a body into a tool result. A body is a fact, not
request-only context.

## Memory

`MEMORY.md` is request context. The `memory` tool appends one bullet and cannot
write other paths. The file is capped to protect the request budget.

## Hooks

`HookRunner` executes configured shell commands around tools. `before_tool` can
deny; `after_tool` observes. Hooks are trusted and time-bounded. See
[Hooks, MCP, and subagents](../hooks-mcp-subagents.md).

## MCP

Each configured stdio server keeps one persistent process. Discovery reads
`tools/list`; calls use `tools/call` over a serialized queue. Tools are prefixed
`mcp__`, ask by default, and are denied in plan and read-only modes. A server
that cannot start is reported and skipped.

## Subagents

`SubagentTool` creates a child session under `<sessions>/subagents`. The child
gets the parent provider, budget, policy, approver, hooks, context, and base
tools plus its own history. It cannot spawn another subagent and is limited to
20 steps. The parent records only the call and summary. `DelegateTool` runs one
or more child tasks sequentially and optionally applies a child mode.

## Snapshots

`SnapshotStore` captures `write`, `edit`, and common single-command shell
mutations. `--undo` and `/undo` restore the latest snapshot. Snapshots are project
state, not session facts.

## Goals

`GoalStore` persists one objective in `.cade-mini/goal.json`. The `goal` tool and
`/goal` command manage it. An active goal is request context.

## Hosts

The CLI runs one-shot and REPL sessions. The web host serves a page and a small
JSON API over one session. Both use the same loop and policy.

## Limits

Extensions are deliberately small. MCP is a stdio client, not a full capability
negotiation implementation. Hooks are shell commands, not in-process callbacks.
Subagents are sequential and share the parent approval context.

## Tests

`test_mini_skills.py`, `test_mini_memory.py`, `test_mini_hooks.py`,
`test_mini_mcp.py`, `test_mini_subagents.py`, `test_mini_snapshots.py`,
`test_mini_goal.py`, and `test_mini_web.py`.

# Tools and security

<!-- source: tools-security.md -->

# Tools and security

## Workspace tools

- `read`: read a UTF-8 file with line numbers. Files are capped.
- `write`: write UTF-8 text and create parent directories.
- `edit`: replace one exact occurrence of old text.
- `glob`: list files matching a workspace glob.
- `grep`: search file contents with a regular expression.
- `bash`: run a shell command in the workspace.

## Context and extension tools

- `history`: retrieve compacted or pruned evidence.
- `skill`: load the full body of an available `SKILL.md`.
- `memory`: append a durable fact to `MEMORY.md`.
- `goal`: read, set, complete, or clear the workspace goal.
- `subagent`: run one child task in its own session.
- `delegate`: run one or more child tasks sequentially, optionally in a mode.
- `mcp__<server>__<tool>`: tools discovered from a configured MCP server.

## Modes

`plan` exposes read, glob, grep, history, skill, and bash. Writes and edits are
hidden and denied. Only classified read-only shell commands are allowed.

`build` exposes all tools. Writes and edits are allowed. Read-only shell
commands are allowed; mutating or unknown commands ask.

`act` exposes all tools. Writes, edits, and shell commands ask.

`--read-only` denies writes, edits, shell commands, memory, and MCP regardless of
mode. It does not block reads, search, history, skills, or goal state.

## Rules and grants

Static rules live in `cade-mini.json`. They are evaluated last match first and
can match tool, path prefix, and command prefix. A hard path boundary always
wins.

A session grant is created when an approval answer is `a` (always). The grant
matches the same tool and the same path or command. `/permissions` lists grants;
`/permissions clear` removes them. Grants last for the process only. Use rules
for durable policy.

## Shell classification

The shell analyzer labels a command as `read_only`, `mutating`, or `unknown`.
It is deliberately conservative:

- `ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `rg`, `git status`, `git diff`, and similar commands are
  read-only.
- `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `git commit`, `python`, and other mutating commands are
  mutating.
- Pipelines, redirections, command lists, substitutions, and unknown binaries
  are unknown.

Plan mode denies unknown commands. Build and act ask.

## Approvals

An ask is answered by:

- `--yes`: approve.
- `--auto-review`: ask the model for `ALLOW` or `DENY`; failures deny.
- Otherwise a TTY prompt: `y` once, `n` deny, `a` always for this exact call.
- Non-TTY without `--yes` or auto-review: deny.

## Process isolation

Cade Mini does not implement an OS sandbox. `bash` runs with the permissions of
the Cade Mini process. The path boundary, modes, shell classification, and
approvals are the safety layer; do not run untrusted commands or repositories
with `--yes`.

## Best practices

- Use `plan` for review and `build` for scoped edits.
- Prefer explicit rules over `--yes` in shared repositories.
- Keep commands simple so the classifier can reason about them.
- Use `--read-only` for inspection-only automation.

# Snapshots and goals

<!-- source: snapshots-goals.md -->

# Snapshots and goals

## File snapshots

Cade Mini records a snapshot before a file tool changes a file. Snapshots live
under `.cade-mini/snapshots` with a JSONL index and one directory per snapshot.

Covered changes:

- `write` and `edit`.
- Common single-command shell mutations: `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `touch`, `mkdir`,
  redirection with `>`, and `sed -i`.
- Creating a file records that it did not exist; undo removes it.

Not covered:

- Complex pipelines, command lists, unknown scripts, and commands that mutate
  files without naming them.
- Files larger than the snapshot limit (5 MiB) are rejected rather than
  silently skipped.
- Directory trees are not copied; directory mutations are skipped.

## Undo

```bash
cade-mini --undo
```

This restores the latest snapshot and exits without contacting a provider. In
the REPL, use `/undo`. Each call restores one snapshot, so repeated undo walks
back through the recorded changes.

Snapshots are project state, not session facts. They are not part of the
JSONL session branch.

## Goals

A goal is one durable objective stored in `.cade-mini/goal.json`. It has an
objective, a status (`active` or `done`), and an update time.

```bash
cade-mini --goal "Add a regression test for the parser" "Start the task."
```

In the REPL:

- `/goal` shows the current goal.
- `/goal TEXT` sets an active goal.
- `/goal done` marks it complete.
- `/goal clear` removes it.

The `goal` tool provides the same actions to the model. An active goal is added
to request context so a resumed or compacted session still knows the objective.
Goals are host state; they do not change the session schema.

Goals are intentionally small. Use `NOTE.md` for working details and `MEMORY.md`
for facts that outlive the objective.

# Skills and memory

<!-- source: skills-memory.md -->

# Skills and memory

## Skills

Cade Mini discovers `SKILL.md` files in two roots:

1. `~/.cade-mini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for user skills.
2. `<project>/.cade-mini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for project skills.

Later roots override earlier roots with the same skill name. A skill file can
start with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: release-check
description: Validate release metadata before tagging.
---

Run the release checklist...
```

`name` defaults to the parent directory. `description` defaults to the first
non-empty body line. Invalid names and empty bodies are skipped.

The request gets a compact `<available-skills>` catalog with names and
descriptions. The model loads a body on demand with the `skill` tool:

```json
{"name": "release-check"}
```

Skill bodies are facts in the tool result, not request-only context. Loading the
same skill twice is harmless but adds another tool result.

## Memory

`MEMORY.md` at the project root stores durable facts. It is loaded into request
context as `<memory source="MEMORY.md">` on every task, capped at 32 KiB.

The model appends facts with the `memory` tool:

```json
{"text": "Prefer pytest and keep changes minimal."}
```

`memory` writes only `MEMORY.md`; it cannot write arbitrary paths. The file is
capped at 64 KiB for writes. Remove stale entries manually when it fills.

Memory is different from the other state files:

- `AGENTS.md` is project instruction, owned by the project.
- `NOTE.md` is short-lived working state; it is summarized with compaction.
- `MEMORY.md` is a durable preference or convention.
- The session log is the record of what happened.

## Request context

Instructions, skill catalog, `NOTE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and an active goal are all
request-only context. They appear in each request audit but never become
conversation messages. See [Sessions and context](sessions-context.md).

# Hooks, MCP, and subagents

<!-- source: hooks-mcp-subagents.md -->

# Hooks, MCP, and subagents

## Hooks

Hooks run shell commands around tools. They are configured in `cade-mini.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "event": "before_tool",
      "command": "python tools/check_tool.py",
      "matcher": "bash",
      "timeout_ms": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```

- `before_tool` runs after policy and approval, before the tool executes. A
  non-zero exit denies the call and records an error tool result.
- `after_tool` runs after a successful or failed executed tool. Its output is
  ignored.
- `matcher` is an exact tool name, a prefix ending in `*`, or omitted for all.
- Commands run with the workspace as the working directory and receive
  `CADE_HOOK_EVENT`, `CADE_TOOL_NAME`, `CADE_TOOL_ARGS`, and
  `CADE_TOOL_RESULT`.

Hooks are trusted configuration. A hook that hangs is killed after its timeout.

## MCP

MCP servers use stdio. Cade Mini starts one persistent process per server and
discovers its tools at startup:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout_ms": 30000
    }
  }
}
```

Tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Their input schema comes from the
server's `tools/list` response. Calls run sequentially over the connection and
preserve server state.

Policy:

- `plan` mode hides MCP tools and denies them.
- `read_only` denies them.
- `build` and `act` ask by default; a rule can allow a specific tool.

A server that fails to start is reported at startup and skipped. Connections
are closed at process exit.

## Subagents

The `subagent` tool runs one child task in its own session and returns the final
answer with the child session ID:

```json
{"prompt": "Find the failing test and report the file and line."}
```

The child:

- gets the parent's provider, budget, policy, approver, hooks, and request
  context;
- gets the base tools plus a history tool bound to its own log;
- does not get another `subagent` tool, so it cannot recurse;
- uses at most 20 steps;
- writes its own session under `<sessions>/subagents/`.

The parent records only the tool call and the returned summary. The child log
keeps the detailed evidence.

`delegate` uses the same runner for one or more tasks:

```json
{"tasks": ["Inspect the parser", "Add a regression test"], "mode": "build"}
```

Tasks run sequentially in separate child sessions. Each result includes the
child session ID; the parent gets one combined tool result.

## Limits

MCP is a small stdio client, not a full capability negotiation implementation.
Hooks are shell commands, not in-process callbacks. Subagents are sequential and
share the parent's approval context rather than running in parallel.

# Cookbook

<!-- source: cookbook/README.md -->

# Cookbook

Procedures with a concrete outcome and a verification step. Each recipe names
the mode and the evidence to keep.

- [Fix a bug](fix-a-bug.md): reproduce, patch, verify, report.
- [Add a feature](add-a-feature.md): test, implement, verify, review the diff.
- [Review only](review-only.md): investigate in plan mode without mutations.
- [Run a long session](long-session.md): NOTE, compaction, history, and goals.
- [Connect a custom MCP server](custom-mcp.md): configure, allow, call, inspect.

For command details, see [CLI](../cli.md) and [Configuration](../configuration.md).

# Fix a bug

<!-- source: cookbook/fix-a-bug.md -->

# Fix a bug

Use `build` mode for the change. Keep the patch minimal and verify with the
repository's tests.

## Procedure

1. Reproduce the failure:

   ```bash
   cade-mini --mode plan "Read the failing test and explain the failure."
   ```

2. Fix it:

   ```bash
   cade-mini --mode build --yes "Fix the failing test with the smallest change, then run pytest."
   ```

3. Inspect the diff and the snapshot:

   ```bash
   git diff
   cade-mini --undo  # only if the change is wrong
   ```

## Verify

- The targeted test passes.
- The full relevant test file passes.
- The diff contains only the intended change.
- The assistant names the command it ran.

## Keep

The run log records the request, tool calls, and test output. The snapshot
allows recovery before the next run. For a reviewable change, keep the diff in
the commit, not in a docs file.

## Avoid

- `--read-only` when you intend to edit.
- `--yes` on a shared repository without rules.
- A broad refactor when a one-line condition fixes the test.

# Add a feature

<!-- source: cookbook/add-a-feature.md -->

# Add a feature

Write the test first, then implement, then verify. Use `build` mode and keep the
diff reviewable.

## Procedure

1. Ask for a failing test or write it yourself:

   ```bash
   cade-mini --mode build --yes "Add a test for mul() that asserts 2 * 3 == 6; run it and confirm it fails."
   ```

2. Implement the smallest change:

   ```bash
   cade-mini --mode build --yes "Implement mul() and run the new test."
   ```

3. Review:

   ```bash
   git diff
   pytest -q
   ```

## Verify

- The new test fails before the change and passes after it.
- Existing tests still pass.
- The implementation has no unrelated edits.
- Public behavior is documented in the relevant guide.

## Undo

If the change is wrong, use `cade-mini --undo` or `/undo` before starting
another attempt. Undo restores one recorded file change at a time.

## Keep

Update the guide or decision record when the feature changes a public contract.
Tests belong in `tests/`; docs belong under `docs/cade-mini/`.

# Review only

<!-- source: cookbook/review-only.md -->

# Review only

Use `plan` and `--read-only` when the task is to inspect, not change.

## Procedure

```bash
cade-mini --mode plan --read-only "Review the request builder for evidence loss. Cite files and lines; do not modify anything."
```

Plan mode hides write and edit tools and denies mutating shell commands.
`--read-only` also denies memory, MCP, and any remaining mutation.

## Verify

- `git status` is clean.
- The answer cites files by relative path and line.
- Claims about tests name the command and result.
- Findings distinguish a bug from a preference.

## Keep

For a review, keep the report in the conversation or a review document. Do not
create a working note unless the review spans multiple sessions.

## Limits

The model can still read anything inside the workspace. A review of untrusted
code still needs human judgment; the policy prevents writes, not misleading
prose.

# Run a long session

<!-- source: cookbook/long-session.md -->

# Run a long session

Long tasks need durable state and a way to recover context. Use `NOTE.md`, a
goal, and the history tool.

## Procedure

1. Set a goal:

   ```bash
   cade-mini --goal "Migrate the request builder to the new budget model" "Start by mapping the current admission rules."
   ```

2. Keep a working note. Ask the model to update `NOTE.md` after each milestone:

   ```text
   Update NOTE.md with completed work, current blockers, and the next action.
   ```

3. Continue the same session:

   ```bash
   cade-mini --continue "Resume from NOTE.md and run the next step."
   ```

4. Compact when the session grows:

   ```text
   /compact
   ```

5. Recover an old detail:

   ```text
   Use history with query "budget" to find the earlier discussion.
   ```

## Verify

- `NOTE.md` names the next action, not just history.
- A resumed run can continue without the original terminal.
- The goal is marked done only when its acceptance check passes.

## Limits

`NOTE.md` is request context and is summarized during compaction. `MEMORY.md` is
for durable facts, not a task log. The session log is the authority for exact
evidence.

# Connect a custom MCP server

<!-- source: cookbook/custom-mcp.md -->

# Connect a custom MCP server

MCP servers use stdio. Cade Mini keeps one process per server and exposes each
tool as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

## Configure

Add the server to `cade-mini.json`:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["tools/mcp_files.py"],
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "env": {"LOG_LEVEL": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

`command` and `args` are required; `cwd`, `env`, and `timeout_ms` are optional.
A relative `cwd` resolves against the project root.

## Allow

MCP tools ask by default. Add a rule for a specific tool if unattended runs need
it:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "mcp__files__read_file", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

Plan mode and `--read-only` deny MCP tools even with a rule.

## Verify

1. Start Cade Mini; it prints a startup error if the server cannot start.
2. Ask the model to list or call a discovered tool.
3. Check the tool result and the `mcp__` prefix in the log.
4. Stop Cade Mini; the server process closes at exit.

## Limits

The client implements `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`. It does not
implement resources, prompts, sampling, or server-initiated requests. A server
that hangs is killed after the configured timeout.

# Hosts

<!-- source: hosts.md -->

# Hosts

Cade Mini has two hosts: the terminal CLI and a local web host. Both use the
same session log, request builder, tools, and policy.

## Terminal

Without a task, the CLI starts a REPL:

```bash
cade-mini
```

The REPL prints tool progress to stderr, streams assistant text to stdout, and
accepts the commands listed in [CLI](cli.md). With a task, it runs once and
exits:

```bash
cade-mini "Fix the failing test."
cade-mini exec "Fix the failing test."
```

One-shot mode supports `--json` for a JSONL event stream. The REPL does not.

## Web

```bash
cade-mini --web --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The page submits tasks and displays the final
answer.

Endpoints:

- `GET /` serves the page.
- `POST /api/task` accepts `{"task": "..."}` and returns the answer,
  termination, steps, error, and session ID.
- `GET /api/sessions` returns the session list.

The web host serves one session for its lifetime. Requests are serialized so two
browser tabs cannot interleave turns.

Security:

- The server binds to loopback by default.
- There is no terminal to answer an approval prompt. Without `--yes` or a rule,
  writes and shell commands are denied while reads still work.
- `--read-only` denies mutations explicitly.

## Choosing a host

Use the terminal for interactive review and approvals. Use the web host for a
small local console or a demo. Use one-shot mode for scripts and CI, with
`--read-only` or explicit rules rather than a blanket `--yes`.

There is no separate TUI workbench. The REPL provides terminal interaction, and
the web host provides a browser surface.

# Development

<!-- source: development.md -->

# Development

## Setup

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra dev
mkdir -p e2e-results
```

Run checks from the repository root:

```bash
uv run --locked ruff check src/cade_mini/ tests/
uv run --locked ruff format --check src/cade_mini/ tests/
uv run --locked pyright src/cade_mini/
uv run --locked pytest -q tests --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
```

For Mini-focused work:

```bash
uv run --locked pytest -q \
  tests/test_mini_log.py \
  tests/test_mini_projection.py \
  tests/test_mini_request.py \
  tests/test_mini_loop.py \
  tests/test_mini_cli.py --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
```

This suite covers only Mini and its owned lower layers; the separate Cade
project has its own tests.

## Documentation

The docs source is `docs/cade-mini/`. The manifest is
`docs/cade-mini/docs.json`; it defines navigation order and which pages are
published.

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs check
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs build
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs llms --write
uv run --locked python -m cade_mini.docs catalogs --write
```

`check` validates the manifest, page files, relative links, and anchors. The CI
workflow runs it without the docs extra, because checking uses only the standard
library.

`build` renders `docs/index.html` from Markdown and the manifest. It needs
`markdown-it-py`, installed by the `docs` extra.

`llms --write` updates `docs/cade-mini/llms.txt` and
`docs/cade-mini/llms-full.txt`. The first is an agent catalog; the second
contains the full page bodies.

### Adding a page

1. Add the Markdown file under `docs/cade-mini/`.
2. Add it to a section in `docs.json`.
3. Use relative links to other pages.
4. Run `python -m cade_mini.docs check`.
5. Regenerate `llms.txt` and the site.

Every Markdown file under `docs/cade-mini/` must be listed in the manifest,
except paths matching `exclude` (decision records are excluded).

### Writing style

- Use active voice and short sentences.
- Lead with the task, then the details.
- Use fenced code blocks with a language.
- Keep commands copy-pasteable.
- State limitations explicitly.

The repository language rules apply: code comments and docstrings are Chinese;
documentation, prompts, and UI text are English.

## Boundaries

Mini owns the provider and process layers in `cade_mini.ai` and
`cade_mini.execution_env`. `tests/test_mini_boundary.py` rejects imports from
the old `cade` namespace. Do not add dependencies on the separate Cade project.

Public interfaces include the session schema, config fields, CLI flags, tool
names, and docs manifest. Change them with tests and documentation in the same
commit.

# Parity

<!-- source: parity.md -->

# Parity

Cade Mini was accepted against Cade on two real repository workflows and a
session resume. The full report is [Cade Mini parity](../cade-mini-parity.md).

## Workflows

Two clean Git repositories started from the same baseline and the same
`AGENTS.md` instruction: "Run pytest after changes. Keep changes minimal."

Bug fix:

- Task: fix `add` in `calc.py` so pytest passes.
- Both agents changed `a - b` to `a + b`, ran pytest, got one passing test, and
  answered `FIXED`.

Feature:

- Task: add `mul(a, b)` and a test.
- Both agents produced the same diff, ran pytest, got two passing tests, and
  answered `PASS`.

Resume:

- Both agents resumed their prior session, recalled `calc.py`, and identified
  the corrected `+` operator.

## Evidence

- Mini ran with `--mode build --yes`; Cade ran with `--mode build --approval
  auto-review`.
- Both used DeepSeek `deepseek-chat`.
- Mini used five steps per workflow; Cade used four. Mini issued an extra `glob`
  inspection, which did not change the result.
- Cade emits JSONL telemetry and budget/approval events; Mini emits human tool
  progress and appends request/run facts to its session log.

## Differences

- Mini's snapshots cover write/edit and common single-command shell mutations;
  complex pipelines are not covered.
- Mini's MCP client is persistent per server but has a narrower capability
  surface than Cade's.
- The OS sandbox is not implemented; Mini relies on path boundaries, modes,
  shell classification, and approvals.
- The live Codex acceptance passed: write created `codex.txt`, and a resumed
  Codex session read it back.

The parity report records the concrete fixtures and observed results. Re-run a
workflow by creating a clean fixture, running both agents with the settings
above, and comparing the diff and test result rather than the prose answer.

# Postmortems

<!-- source: postmortem/README.md -->

# Postmortems

A postmortem records an incident that escaped the intended design. It is the
only place for chronology and war stories; current behavior belongs in the
subsystem reference.

## Records

- [0001: Compaction cut pointed at a shadowed user entry](0001-compaction-cut-misalignment.md)
- [0002: One huge tool result exhausted the request budget](0002-single-huge-tool-result.md)

## Template

Copy [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md). Keep the timeline factual, name the root cause,
show the fix, and record the test that would have caught it. Do not turn the
postmortem into a tutorial; link the current behavior page instead.

Postmortems are excluded from the published guide manifest but remain valid
links and are reviewed with the fix.

# 0001: Compaction cut pointed at a shadowed user entry

<!-- source: postmortem/0001-compaction-cut-misalignment.md -->

# 0001: Compaction cut pointed at a shadowed user entry

Date: 2026-10-18

Status: resolved

## Impact

After a prior compaction, the next compaction could choose a `first_kept_id`
from a user entry that was already shadowed. The summary covered the wrong tail,
and the retained window could omit the current task.

## Timeline

- The compactor collected all user entries from the branch.
- It collected user positions from the visible projection.
- It chose a cut by visible position but indexed the full branch entry list.
- A session with a prior compaction therefore pointed at an older, shadowed
  user entry.

## Root cause

Two lists with different lengths were treated as parallel arrays. A compaction
removes old user entries from the projection but leaves them in the branch. The
index into visible positions is not an index into all branch users.

## Fix

The compactor now aligns with the **last N** user entries, where N is the number
of visible user messages. A regression test builds a session with a prior
summary, a retained turn, and a new task, then asserts the new cut points at the
new task and the summary request contains the prior summary.

## Verification

`test_mini_compaction.py::test_iterative_compaction_includes_prior_summary`
passes. The projected roles are `system, summary, user`.

## Follow-up

Any future cut logic must derive entry IDs from the same visible sequence it uses
to choose positions. See [Context and compaction](../subsystems/context-compaction.md).

# 0002: One huge tool result exhausted the request budget

<!-- source: postmortem/0002-single-huge-tool-result.md -->

# 0002: One huge tool result exhausted the request budget

Date: 2026-10-18

Status: resolved

## Impact

A single tool result larger than the input budget could make a request
impossible. The request builder protected the most recent four tool results, so
a lone huge result was never replaced, and the run ended with `context_error`.

## Timeline

- A tool returned a result larger than the budget.
- Admission protected the result because it was among the latest four.
- Turn dropping removed old turns but not the current turn's huge result.
- The request remained over budget and the run failed.

## Root cause

The pruning policy treated "recent" as always protected. Protection is a
heuristic for preserving working evidence, not a hard invariant. With only one
result, the protected set was the entire candidate set.

## Fix

Admission now prunes in passes:

1. Replace unprotected results, oldest first.
2. If still over, replace protected results oldest first.
3. If still over, replace the newest result as a last resort.

Every replacement points to the history tool, so the evidence remains
retrievable. A regression test covers a single huge result.

## Verification

`test_mini_request.py::test_build_prunes_a_single_huge_tool_result` passes and
the resulting request is under budget.

## Follow-up

Keep the history tool available whenever pruning can remove the newest result.
See [Projection and request](../subsystems/projection-request.md).

# Persistence

<!-- source: persistence/README.md -->

# Persistence

Cade Mini has one durable conversation format: the session log. The rest are
host-state files with narrow scopes.

## Current format

- Session log: schema v1, closed. See [Session log schema](../../cade-mini-schema.md).
- Entry file: one JSON object per line; a trailing newline is required.
- Session directory: `.cade-mini/sessions`.
- Compaction and windows are entries, not file rewrites.
- Snapshots, goals, NOTE, memory, and config are separate artifacts.

## Compatibility

A reader must reject an unknown schema version rather than guess. A writer must
not add fields that change the meaning of existing fields. Additive diagnostic
fields are allowed only when old readers can ignore them.

## History

There are no format migrations yet. When the first change lands, add a record
under [upgrade](../upgrade/README.md) and a decision record describing the
migration and rollback.

## Verification

`test_mini_log.py`, `test_mini_projection.py`, and
`test_mini_acceptance.py` exercise the current format. A schema change must add a
test that opens an old fixture and one that rejects a future version.

## Related

- [Persistence catalog](../design/persistence-catalog.md)
- [Change policy](change-policy.md)
- [Session log schema](../../cade-mini-schema.md)

# Change policy

<!-- source: persistence/change-policy.md -->

# Change policy

A persisted format change is a public interface change. It needs a decision,
tests, and a migration path.

## Before changing the schema

1. Write a decision record under `docs/cade-mini/decisions/`.
2. State whether the change is additive, transformative, or breaking.
3. Describe how an old session is read and whether it is rewritten.
4. Define the new schema version and the reader's rejection rule.
5. Add an old-format fixture and a migration test.

## Rules

- Never rewrite a user's session file in place without an explicit migration.
- Never infer a missing field from a provider's current behavior.
- Keep audit facts out of the projection unless the schema says otherwise.
- Bump the version for any change that an old reader cannot ignore.
- Update [Persistence](README.md), the [schema](../../cade-mini-schema.md), and
  the [upgrade guide](../upgrade/README.md) in the same change.

## Review checklist

- Old fixture opens and projects identically.
- Unknown future version fails with a clear error.
- Migration is idempotent and can be interrupted.
- New fields have a documented owner and lifetime.
- Session size and compaction behavior remain bounded.

## Current status

Schema v1 is closed. No migration exists. The next format change must add the
first entry to the upgrade guide.

# Upgrade guide

<!-- source: upgrade/README.md -->

# Upgrade guide

This page records changes that require action from an existing user or
automation.

## Standalone project

Cade Mini now installs as `cade-mini`, with Python imports under `cade_mini`.
The old `cade` command and `cade.mini` namespace are removed. No compatibility
or migration tools are provided.

Authenticate again with `cade-mini login`. Credentials and skills use
`~/.cade-mini/`; project skills use `.cade-mini/skills/`. Mini no longer
reads `.cade` directories. Session schema v1 remains the current format.

## When an upgrade is needed

An upgrade entry is required when:

- the session schema version changes;
- a config key is renamed or removed;
- a CLI flag changes meaning;
- a tool name or parameter becomes incompatible;
- a persisted host-state file changes shape.

## Procedure for a future upgrade

1. Read the relevant decision record.
2. Back up `.cade-mini/` before migrating.
3. Run the documented migration command once.
4. Open a session and verify the projection and `history` tool.
5. Keep the old directory until the new version has passed a real task.

## Compatibility promise

Additive optional config fields are not breaking. A new event type is breaking
because the schema is closed. A removed tool or a changed parameter is breaking.
The change policy is in [Persistence](../persistence/change-policy.md).
